name: Kedah-Perak Malay
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Shahidi A.H. 2009, Alternasi Dalam Fonologi Subdialek Kedah Utara, Jurnal Bahasa 9(2):302-325

sources.citation: Shahidi A.H., Ain Atiqah Latiff, Muhammad Syahmi Syabri, Muhamad Faiz Fauzi & Riduan Makhtar. 2020. Penelitian akustik dialek Kedah. Jurnal Melayu, Isu Khas Disember 2020, pp. 577ff.
sources.note: Acoustic (VOT, closure duration, voicing) study of bilabial plosives in Kedah Malay vs Standard Malay; no stress or F0-prominence analysis; the only suprasegmental remark is a literature note on nasalization studies.

sources.citation: W. E. Maxwell. 1914 [1882]. A manual of the Malay language, with an introductory sketch of the Sanskrit element in Malay (10th ed.). London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner.
sources.note: Preface (p. vi): 'The Kedah accent is easily distinguished from that of Patani'; Introduction (p. 4): Malay 'probably spoken with greatest purity in the states of Kedah and Perak'; no stress-placement rule anywhere (grep for accent/stress/syllable/penult yields nothing relevant).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kedah Malay' (en) and 'Bahasa Melayu Kedah' (ms), raw wikitext fetched sources 2026-09-17
sources.note: Consonant/vowel tables only; no stress section; cites Shahidi 2009 via myjurnal.mohe.gov.my (id 66566), which refuses connections from our machine.

sources.citation: Mohammad Khairulanwar Abdul Ghani & Mohd Tarmizi Hasrah. 2025. Sejarah fonologi dialek Melayu Hulu Kedah. Jurnal Bahasa 25(1):1-40. doi:10.37052/jb25(1)no1
sources.note: Historical phonology of Hulu Kedah (Baling) Malay: proto-phoneme reflexes, vowels, consonants, syllable structure; nothing on stress (grep for tekanan/stress/suprasegmen/aksen/intonasi finds only 'penekanan' = 'emphasis' in prose).

sources.citation: Mohammad Khairulanwar bin Abdul Ghani. 2025. Dialek Melayu Hulu Kedah: satu analisis sinkronik dan diakronik. PhD thesis, Universiti Utara Malaysia. https://etd.uum.edu.my/11997/
sources.note: Only the open part (front matter, abstract, table of contents, chapter 1, references, wordlist; 62 pp.) could be fetched sources; the full text  is under a 3-year embargo (HTTP 401). Chapter 4 'Pemerian fonem' is in the embargoed part. No stress statement in the open part; its bibliography lists the Kedah phonology literature used for the wishlist.

sources.citation: Muhammad Khairulanwar Abd. Ghani & Mohd Tarmizi Hasrah. 2024. Rekonstruksi dalaman dialek Baling purba. RENTAS: Jurnal Bahasa, Sastera dan Budaya 3:209-232. doi:10.32890/rentas2024.3.10
sources.note: Internal reconstruction of Baling Malay segments; no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Shahidi A.H., Mohamad Firdaus Azaharuddin & Rahim Aman. 2024. Selayang pandang kajian variasi dialek Melayu berasaskan kaedah tradisi dan moden. Jurnal Melayu 23(1).
sources.note: Survey of Malay dialect-variation studies; only suprasegmental remark concerns phonemic consonant length in Patani Malay; nothing on Kedah/Perak stress.

sources.citation: Shahidi A.H., Nurul Huda Ariffin & Rahim Aman. 2021. Dialek Perak varian Kuala Kangsar: satu pemerian fonetik akustik. Jurnal Melayu, Isu Khas Disember 2021, pp. 602ff.
sources.note: Acoustics of plosive voicing in Perak Malay (Kampung Sayong, Kuala Kangsar); 'tekanan (stress)' occurs only in a review of English closure-duration studies (Stathopoulos & Weismer 1983 etc.); nothing on Perak Malay stress placement.

sources.citation: Ong Su Teck, Nur Syahida Adilah Suri & Rahim Aman. 2016. Fonologi subdialek Pulau Pinang: satu kajian di Balik Pulau. e-Bangi: Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities 11(1):186-201.
sources.note: Segmental phonology (vowel/consonant distribution, diphthongs) of a Penang subdialect of Kedah Malay; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Norfazila Ab. Hamid & Rahim Aman. 2014. Proses pemanjangan vokal dalam dialek Hulu Sik Kedah: satu penerapan teori fonologi generatif model non-linear. e-Bangi 9(2):195-205.
sources.note: Compensatory vowel lengthening in Hulu Sik (Kedah) speech analysed autosegmentally; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Zaharani Ahmad, Nor Hashimah Jalaluddin & Shariffulizan Malek. 2011. Fonologi rangkap vokal dan kepelbagaian dialek Melayu: analisis teori optimaliti. GEMA Online Journal of Language Studies 11(3).
sources.note: OT treatment of vowel sequences in Johor, Kedah, Perak and Kelantan dialects (foot constraint KT>=KAKI used for syllabification); no statement on stress placement.

sources.citation: Zaharani b. Ahmad. 1991. The phonology and morphology of the Perak dialect. Kuala Lumpur: Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (Siri Kajian Bahasa), xviii+175 pp.
